html:
SMTO-CFG-0107 — SMTO's settings file has a value it can't accept

GUID: 39b1e9fc-4d86-48c6-ae33-d7267909c16c
Slug: bootstrap-configuration-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: startup

What happened

  • SMTO read its startup settings, but one setting has the wrong kind of value or is out of range, such as text where a number belongs. SMTO stopped before opening your saved data, so nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the startup screen, open Technical details. It lists each setting to fix and what it needs, for example llm.max_tokens: Use an integer. SMTO hides the wrong value for safety but names the setting and the rule it must follow.
  2. Open SMTO's settings file: the file given with --config, the file named by AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH, or config.yaml in the folder SMTO starts from. Correct that setting. This is the file SMTO checks before anything else starts.
  3. If the setting isn't in that file, look for a matching AOR_ setting in the script or service that starts SMTO, and correct it there. Startup settings can also come from the way SMTO is launched.
  4. Select Start again on the startup screen if you see it, or start SMTO the way you normally do. SMTO reads its settings again only when it starts.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen moves past the settings check and reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the setting names shown under Technical details, to the person who installed SMTO. Don't turn off password, HTTPS or certificate checks to get past this; they aren't the cause.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Bootstrap configuration failed type, range or allowed-option validation for a field in the app config file or AOR_* settings, before runtime storage was opened.

What this means

  • Startup validates bootstrap settings before opening runtime storage. The listed field and accepted constraint come from schema validation; rejected values are omitted. A YAML document can parse successfully and still fail these requirements.

Why this can happen

  • Schema constraints reject invalid field types, missing required fields, unsupported options, and values outside supported ranges.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the named field and accepted constraint; values and nested arbitrary dictionary keys are not copied into this diagnostic.

How to fix it

  • Use the field and requirement list under Technical details (configuration_issues) to correct the --config file, the AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH target or ./config.yaml, or the matching AOR_* environment variable, then restart. Rejected values are deliberately omitted. When running doctor against a live Server, check its effective saved settings; bootstrap values don't override saved controls.
  • SMTO user: correct the listed field in the explicit --config file or AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH source. Use the displayed type or range, then restart. If using doctor against a controller, check its effective settings instead of assuming bootstrap values override saved controls.

Retry and execution caution

  • Restart after the bootstrap configuration validates.

How to verify the fix

  • Bootstrap validation completes and startup advances to runtime ownership/storage initialization.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • Explicit --config takes precedence over AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH and an optional working-directory configuration file.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
